method: Hand input, one rater (the report's author). For every marker whose referenced GitHub issues were all closed as completed or merged at the pinned commit (todo-issues.cjs candidates), the marker's code at the pinned commit was read in the corpus clone and the issue or PR read with gh (read-only). Verdicts: stale (the task is done or the condition it waits for has happened), still valid (the reference is context, or the task doesn't depend on the issue being closed), unclear.

items.evidence: The marker's own condition is the next major version: 'remove in Astro 8'. packages/astro/package.json at the pinned commit is 7.3.8. #18267 ('security.checkOrigin: 7.3.6 checks every Content-Type, docs still say only form-like Content-Types are checked') was closed two days before the pinned commit; the link explains the restored check.
#7529 ('CSS HMR is broken on 2.7.2', closed 2023) is the regression the slower check prevents. The marker asks for a faster approach that doesn't regress it; the code is the same isImportedBy check.

#7348 ('feat: multiplayer undo / redo', merged 2024) is the PR that introduced the marker. It records a known limitation of the new history ('we could still get an empty undo/redo') that the code still has.
Follow-up from #7348 (merged 2024): changed elements are still not validated before being applied.
Follow-up from #7348 (merged 2024): the condition it asks to remove (only text elements are rebound) is still there.
Follow-up from #7348 (merged 2024): invisible elements are still marked deleted and recorded by the store.
Same marker and code as actionFinalize.tsx:156, in the second finalize path.
Follow-up from #7348 (merged 2024): captureUpdate still captures everything when committing.

webpack/webpack#11467 (closed 2020) ended with webpack's maintainers recommending exactly this rule ({ test: /\.m?js/, resolve: { fullySpecified: false } }) and pinning the issue; webpack 5 is the only webpack Next.js supports. The marker ('do NOT webpack 5 support with this') asks for nothing a maintainer can act on now, but the override itself is still needed.
The FIXME on the same comment line as the TODO above; same verdict.
The marker asks for a test of a failing CORS fetch and links #43605 (closed 2023) only for a reproduction. Whether the test exists can't be checked from the sparse clone (test/ isn't in it).

The condition is met: 'Remove from dependencies once https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/29665 is released.' The PR was merged on 2024-07-06, and its merge commit (1b0132c0) is an ancestor of the v19.0.0 tag (gh api compare v19.0.0...1b0132c0: behind by 657, ahead by 0). React 19.0.0 was released in December 2024; `dispatch` is still in the dependency array at the pinned commit.
facebook/react#22644 ('useId', merged 2021) is cited as background for the isomorphic wrapper; the marker's doubt about enhanceApp/enhanceComponents doesn't depend on it.
#89478 ('Don't insert build id comment in HTML', merged 2026) is what made the commented-out stream unused. The marker waits for 'proper output:export support', which the PR didn't add.
